reference.title: Standing Calf Raise (female)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Calves, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you rise, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, 0.8 s pause, 1.8 s down

prescription.progression: Single-leg calf raise, then a step edge for more range, then added load

cues.text: Stand tall facing a wall, feet hip width, toes forward, fingertips resting lightly on the wall.
Breathe out and rise onto the balls of the feet as high as you can.
Pause at the top; weight over the big and second toes, ankles not rolling out.
Breathe in and lower the heels slowly to the floor.

mistakes.fix: Rise as high as you can; activity rises with heel height (Fujisawa 2015).
Keep the pressure over the big and second toes.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning on the wall or bending the knees
mistakes.fix: Fingertips only for balance; stay tall and rise straight up.

kinematics.norm: Rise as high as possible; heel-raise activity rises with height, and active standing plantarflexion range averaged about 50 degrees in young men (Fujisawa 2015)
Standing heel-rise height was about 9-11 cm in a small study (Zellers 2019, machine heel raise on a step)
Feet hip width, toes forward (clinical opinion)
Fujisawa 2015 used 1 s up and 1 s down; a slower lowering is common in training (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #301812, Standing Calf Raise (female), video (movement reference)
Fujisawa et al. 2015, ankle plantar flexor activity in the double-leg heel raise and walking (J Phys Ther Sci 27(5):1523-1526; PMC4483433)
Zellers et al. 2019, seated and standing heel raises and triceps surae activation after Achilles tendon rupture (Transl Sports Med 3(1):3-8; PMC7236791)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Good balance: hands at the sides or on the hips, no wall.
Achilles pain: smaller range and slower, as advised by a clinician.

muscleNotes.calves_r: Gastrocnemius and soleus lift the heels. Plantar flexor activity rose with heel height in the double-leg heel raise (Fujisawa 2015); standing heel raises drew more gastrocnemius activity than seated ones (Zellers 2019).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Gastrocnemius and soleus lift the heels. Plantar flexor activity rose with heel height in the double-leg heel raise (Fujisawa 2015); standing heel raises drew more gastrocnemius activity than seated ones (Zellers 2019).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Keep the knees straight but not locked (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Keep the knees straight but not locked (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis and knees steady over the feet (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis and knees steady over the feet (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the body tall so it rises straight up (clinical opinion).
